These answers are representative. Award credit for physical-system interpretation, student-generated idealization, correct free-body diagrams, wire-force calculations, axial elongations, displacement compatibility, vertical displacement, tilt angles, and a concise engineering assessment.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The unsolved common model and all ten assigned inputs appear after Q10. Q8 remains an independent idealization task; completed free bodies and representative answers are instructor-only. The endpoint-supported rigid members have A below H and B below C. P is an assigned downward load increment on the ideal unstrained, massless reference model. All suspension members have the assigned axial EA; this is not documented rope/chain assembly stiffness.

Use signed rotations, numerical zero/tie rules and weighted wire-elongation contributions to the load-point displacement. Recompute both tilts for load relocation or selective compliance changes. The null strain/rotation screens leave a normal instructional packet explicitly unassessed; a gross finite-segment inconsistency blocks ordinary answer generation and export. Passing that gross check does not establish small-deformation validity or service fitness.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

Suggested weighting:

- context interpretation: 15%;
- idealization: 15%;
- equilibrium: 25%;
- deformation: 25%;
- compatibility and tilt: 15%;
- engineering decision: 5%.
